findings.title: Team admin permission check requires being both admin and owner
findings.body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. Because owners are also admins, this reduces to 'is owner', so regular team ADMIN members are rejected with FORBIDDEN even though the variable name and intent are 'admin or owner'. The operator should be `||`. Team admins see these bookings in the list and get a permission error when they try the action.

findings.title: Notification uses raw request guests instead of the filtered uniqueGuests
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` receives the original request list, while the DB insert uses `uniqueGuests` (existing attendees and blacklisted emails removed). In `sendAddGuestsEmails`, any attendee whose email is in `newGuests` gets the full AttendeeScheduledEmail (booking confirmation) instead of the add-guests notice. So an email the user re-submits that is already an attendee receives a confirmation it should not get. The function should receive `uniqueGuests`.

findings.title: Duplicate guests are not rejected on the server, and existing-attendee match is case-sensitive
findings.body: The filter compares `guest === attendee.email` exactly, so 'A@x.com' is not treated as a duplicate of 'a@x.com'. Nothing dedupes entries inside the `guests` array itself, so a request with the same address twice (or two case variants) creates two Attendee rows via `createMany`. The uniqueness check exists only in the client dialog (the zod refine in AddGuestsDialog), and the server schema (addGuests.schema.ts) does not enforce it. Duplicate attendees then get duplicate invitations and emails.

findings.title: Guest blacklist is bypassed by changing the case of the email
findings.body: `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` entries are lowercased when parsed, but the incoming `guest` is compared as-is with `includes(guest)`. An address such as 'Blocked@Example.com' passes when the list contains 'blocked@example.com', and the guest is then stored and invited. Guests should be normalized (lowercased and trimmed) before both the blacklist and duplicate checks.

findings.title: Calendar update runs with the caller's credentials, not the organizer's
findings.body: The EventManager is built from `ctx.user` and that user's credentials. But `booking.references` and the destination calendar belong to the organizer (`booking.userId`). When the caller is a team admin or a matching attendee rather than the organizer, `updateCalendarAttendees` uses the caller's calendars against the organizer's calendar event, so the new guests are not added to the organizer's calendar or the update fails. The handler already loads `booking.user` with `credentials: true` (line 38) and never uses it.

findings.title: Guests are committed to the DB before the calendar update, with no rollback
findings.body: The attendees are written at line 92, then `updateCalendarAttendees` runs at line 165 outside any transaction. If the calendar call throws, the new attendee rows stay in the database, the mutation returns an error, and the notification emails at line 168 are never sent. On retry, the same guests now match existing attendees and the request fails with 'emails_must_be_unique_valid', so the state cannot be repaired from the UI. The calendar update and notifications need to be ordered or wrapped so a failure does not leave partial state.

findings.title: Email failure is swallowed with a plain console.log and the error object is dropped
findings.body: The catch block logs a fixed string with `console.log` and ignores `err`. The cause of a failed notification is lost, and the mutation still reports 'Guests added'. The error should be logged with the project logger and the error object included.

findings.title: No booking status or time check; guests can be added to cancelled, rejected, or past bookings
findings.body: After loading the booking, the handler checks only permissions. It does not reject cancelled or rejected bookings, or bookings that have already ended. The UI only offers the action for confirmed upcoming bookings, but the API accepts any booking id. A request for a cancelled booking still writes attendees, updates the calendar event, and sends 'guests added' emails for an event that is no longer happening.

findings.title: Unbounded guest list enables email spam to all attendees and the organizer
findings.body: `guests` has no max length, and no rate limit applies. Every successful call sends an email to every existing attendee and the organizer (and team members). Any user who passes the permission check can add an arbitrary number of guests in one call and repeat the call, causing mass invitations sent from the platform. The handler's attendee branch (line 52 of addGuests.handler.ts) also lets any booking attendee, not only the organizer or an admin, trigger this. A maximum array size and a per-booking attendee cap should be enforced.

findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores event-type disableStandardEmails settings
findings.body: Every other send function in this file takes `eventTypeMetadata` and checks `eventTypeDisableHostEmail` / `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail`. `sendAddGuestsEmails` takes no metadata and always emails the organizer, team members, and attendees. Event types that disable standard emails will still send 'guests added' emails. The handler also does not pass the event type metadata.

findings.title: New guest records are assigned the organizer's timezone and locale
findings.body: Each new attendee is stored with `timeZone: organizer.timeZone` and `locale: organizer.locale`. The guest's real timezone and locale are unknown, but these values are persisted as if they were the guest's, and later drive how that guest's emails and calendar invites are rendered. Storing a neutral default or leaving the value unset would be more accurate.

findings.title: Error message is misleading when guests are filtered out as existing or blacklisted
findings.body: When every submitted guest is already an attendee or is blacklisted, the handler throws 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' ('Emails must be unique and valid'). That text describes a format or duplicate-input error, not 'these addresses are already on the booking' or 'these addresses are blocked'. Blacklisted entries that are mixed with valid ones are dropped silently with no indication to the caller.

findings.title: No tests for addGuests authorization, filtering, or notification logic
findings.body: The new handler has a non-trivial permission matrix (organizer, team admin/owner, attendee), a filtering step (existing attendees, blacklist, duplicates), and a calendar and email side effect. None of it is covered by a test in this PR. The inverted admin/owner condition noted above is the kind of bug a basic handler test would catch.

findings.title: Fallback error message is unreachable and the error text includes the raw error code
findings.body: `message` is a template string that always contains a non-empty `${err.data?.code}: ...` prefix, so `message || t("unable_to_add_guests")` never falls back. The user also sees raw codes such as 'FORBIDDEN: you_do_not_have_permission' or 'BAD_REQUEST: ...'. The fallback should be applied to the translated message, not to the concatenation.

findings.title: Dialog state persists across open/close, so a stale validation error and old entries reappear
findings.body: `isInvalidEmail` is set to true on a failed client validation, but `onSuccess` never resets it. Closing the dialog through Escape or the overlay (`onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}`) also skips the reset in the Cancel button, so the old emails and the error message remain. When the dialog is reopened, the user sees the stale error and previously entered addresses, which can then trigger the duplicate error on a retry.

findings.title: Hardcoded English tooltip string bypasses i18n
findings.body: The remove-email tooltip uses the literal string "Remove email" instead of `t(...)`, so it is not translated, even though this component already uses `t` for its other labels.
